chapter_theme: One song at Someechuram (சோமீச்சுரம்): after a full description of lovemaking the poet asks for the jnana to recite Murugan's youth, beauty, arms, feet and faces even in union, in sleep and in every conversation; the praise tells Prahlada's story.

870.reading: The poet describes lovemaking in detail, hair loosened, face sweating, breasts thrilling, lips like nectar, bangles ringing, two bodies made one without shame, and asks that even while he sinks in union with young women, without a blink, while he sleeps at night or talks with anyone, he be given the knowledge to recite Murugan's youth, beauty, twelve arms, two feet and six faces. The praise tells how, when a child chanted 'Nama Narayanaya' and his father raged 'where is your god?', Vishnu burst from the pillar as a lion and tore Hiranya's chest with his claws, and names Murugan who dwells gladly in the Somesar temple among dancing peacocks and areca groves, by the camp of the Marutha kings.
870.nuance: As in 855, the plea is not to stop but to remember in every state: in union, in sleep, in speech (கலவிதனில் மூழ்கி ஆழுகினும் இமையாதே இரவினிடை துயிலுகினும் யாரோடு பேசுகினும்). Prahlada is unnamed but the story is unmistakable: the child's நமநாராயணாய, the father's question, the pillar and the claws. மருதரசர் படைவிடுதி, the camp of the Marutha kings, is an allusion not identified here.

links.note: Both ask not to escape the women but to keep Murugan in mind amid them; 870 widens it to every state, union, sleep and talk, and asks for the knowledge to recite him.

870 tells how a child chanting 'Nama Narayanaya' was asked by his raging father where his god was, and Vishnu burst from the pillar as a lion and tore Hiranya's chest with his claws (உகிர் புதைய இரணியனை மார்பீறி). 872 tells the same from the pillar Hiranya struck (கனகன் அங்கையினால் அறை தூணிடை), adding that the Man-Lion drank his blood like nectar. The two songs between them give the Narasimha story whole, the child's chant in one and the blood in the other, both in praise of Murugan's uncle.

source_issues: Song 870: corrupt character in §ல்முழ்கி (line 7), probably a word for flood or sea with மூழ்கி; உ ரிய, உ ரமுடைய, உ கிர், உ வணபதி (lines 11 to 14) are split by a space after உ.
